The QA auto-tests also expect:

Bots got popular, and some members create far too many of them:

> As an administrator, I want to cap how many bots each member can have.

The account settings page (`/account/edit`) gets a new setting for administrators:

- "Bots per member" (a number, 5 by default)

Rules:

- A member can have at most that many bots. Deleted bots don't count.
- Administrators are not limited.
- At the limit, the bots page doesn't offer "Add a chat bot" and tells the member they've "reached the limit". Any other attempt to create a bot is refused, too.
- Lowering the limit never removes existing bots; it only blocks new ones.

# Campfire

Campfire is a web-based chat application. It supports many of the features you'd
expect, including:

- Multiple rooms, with access controls
- Direct messages
- File attachments with previews
- Search
- Notifications (via Web Push)
- Chat bots that post messages over HTTP, and that get a webhook when they're mentioned or join a room (see [bots](docs/bots.md))
- @mentions

## Running your own Campfire instance

Campfire's Docker image contains everything needed for a fully-functional,
single-machine deployment. This includes the web app, background jobs, caching,
file serving, and SSL. You can use our pre-built image at
`ghcr.io/basecamp/once-campfire:latest`, or build your own from this repo.

### Deploying with ONCE

The easiest way to self-host Campfire is with [ONCE](https://github.com/basecamp/once).
It will guide you through the initial set up and then keep your instance up to date automatically.

If you don't already have `once` installed, run this on the machine you want to run Campfire on:

```sh
curl https://get.once.com | sh
```

`once` will launch as soon as the install is finished. 

Choose Campfire from the list of applications, follow the instructions, and ONCE will take care of the rest.

If you prefer the command line to the dashboard, you can deploy directly:

```sh
once deploy ghcr.io/basecamp/once-campfire --host chat.example.com
```

### Deploying with Docker

If you'd rather run the Docker image yourself, you can read more about that in the [self-hosting guide](docs/self-hosting.md).

> [!TIP]
> When you start Campfire for the first time, you'll be guided through a wizard to create an admin account.
> The email address that you enter for the admin account will be visible on the sign-in page, it's there so
> that people have someone to contact if they need help with their account. If that bothers you, put in any
> email address you want and create yourself a new admin account.

## Development

You are welcome - and encouraged - to modify Campfire to your liking.
Please see our [development guide](docs/development.md) for how to get Campfire set up for local development.

## Security

See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for how to report a vulnerability and a description of our trust model.
# How to contribute to Campfire

Campfire uses GitHub
[discussions](https://github.com/basecamp/once-campfire/discussions) to track
feature requests and questions, rather than [the issue
tracker](https://github.com/basecamp/once-campfire/issues). If you're considering
opening an issue or pull request, please open a discussion instead.

Whenever a discussion leads to an actionable and well-understood task, we'll
move it to the issue tracker where it can be worked on.

This is a little different than how some other projects work, but it makes it
easier for us to triage and prioritise the work. It also means that the open

```

`once` will launch as soon as the install is finished. 

Choose Campfire from the list of applications, follow the instructions, and ONCE will take care of the rest.

If you prefer the command line to the dashboard, you can deploy directly:

```sh
once deploy ghcr.io/basecamp/once-campfire --host chat.example.com

A bot is set up by a chat member and then driven by a shell script or CI job, which authenticates with the bot's code. ## Setting up a bot (people) 1. Open account settings (`/account/edit`) and click the bot icon, "Set up chat bots" (`/bots`). 2. "Add a chat bot" opens `/bots/new`. The bot name is required. The avatar, the webhook URL and the "Add to all open rooms" switch are optional. The switch is off by default (see below). "Save changes" creates the bot and returns to `/bots`. (Webhooks are described below.) 3. Each bot on the list shows its name and its **bot code** in a read-only "Bot code" field. Copy it into your script or CI secrets. Treat it like a password. 4. "Edit " changes the name and avatar. "Delete this chat bot" (with a confirmation) removes the bot. Who sees and manages what: - Any chat member can create bots. A member sees, edits and deletes only the bots they created. - Administrators see and manage every bot. - The bots page lists all of them on one page (no pagination). - Bots are left out of the people list on the account page, since they're managed from `/bots`. Bots do not join open rooms by default, unlike people. The "Add to all open rooms" switch makes a bot a member of every open room: the rooms that exist when the switch is turned on, and each open room created later. Turning the switch off keeps the bot in the rooms it is already in, and only stops new open rooms from adding it. Bots can be added to closed rooms the same way people are (the access switches in the room's settings). A bot that is not in a room can't post there: the message endpoint answers `404 Not Found` (see "Posting messages"). ## Posting messages (bots) The raw request body is the message. There is no JSON envelope and there are no field names: ```sh curl -d "Deploy of v1.2.3 finished ✅" \ https://chat.example.com/rooms///messages ``` | Response | When | | --- | --- | | `201 Created`, `Location: /messages/:message_id` | The message was posted. | | `422 Unprocessable Content` | The body is empty or only whitespace, or it isn't valid UTF-8. | | `404 Not Found` | The room doesn't exist, or the bot isn't a member of it. | | `401 Unauthorized` (with `WWW-Authenticate: Bot realm="Campfire"`) | The bot code is unknown, the bot was deleted, or its user was deactivated or banned. | Details: - The body is text, whatever `Content-Type` the client sends. `curl -d` sends form encoding by default, and that doesn't change the message: `Disk at 100% done` is posted as written. - Line breaks are kept. Markup is shown as text, so `` in a message appears literally. - Attachments aren't supported. The body is the whole message. - The message shows the bot's name as its author. It's broadcast to the room, updates unread markers, and triggers push notifications exactly like a person's message. - `Location` is `/messages/:id`, as specified. Messages are room-scoped in this app, so that URL returns 404 today. A future change could resolve it to the room's message. ## Receiving mentions (webhooks) A bot can have a **webhook URL**, set in the "Webhook URL" field on `/bots/new` or the bot's edit page. When a person mentions the bot (`@Deploy Bot`) in a message, Campfire POSTs the mention to that URL. The bot answers either in the HTTP response, or later by posting through its bot code. Leaving the field empty removes the webhook. The request is `POST ` with `Content-Type: application/json`: ```json { "event": "mention", "author": { "id": 7, "name": "Alice" }, "room": { "id": 5, "name": "Ops", "reply_to": "/rooms/5//messages" }, "message": { "id": 118, "body": { "text": "restart the build please", "html": "
… full rich-text body …
" }, "link": "/rooms/5/@118" } } ``` - `event` is `mention` for a mention. A bot is also told when it joins a room, with the `joined` event (see "Joining rooms"). - `message.body.text` is the message as text, with the bot's own @mention taken out, so it reads as the command addressed to the bot. Other mentions read as `@Name`. - `message.body.html` is the whole rich-text body, cleaned the way the room cleans messages. Mentions are `action-text-attachment` elements, and their `sgid` identifies the person mentioned. - `room.reply_to` is the bot's own posting URL for that room. POST text to it to reply later (see "Posting messages"). - `message.link` opens the room scrolled to the message. - Paths are relative. The bot knows its Campfire origin, so `https://chat.example.com` plus `reply_to` is the URL. - In a direct message room, `room.name` is the other people in it. The bot replies with: | Response | Result | | --- | --- | | `200` with `Content-Type: text/plain` | The body is posted into the room as the bot's ", "output_tail": "ten it, so bots can't create mentions. **The bot code in the payload.** `room.reply_to` contains the bot code, so the webhook's recipient learns it. That's intended: the webhook is the bot. Apart from the bots page, that's the only place the code leaves Campfire, and the payload is never logged. **Webhook URLs are secrets** (they often carry a token in the path or query). The parameter filter masks `webhook_url` in request logs and in `inspect`, and the bot's edit page isn't cached. **Authorization.** Editing and deleting use `Current.user.can_administer?(bot)`, which means administrator or creator, the same rule used for other records here. ## Protecting bot codes A bot code grants the ability to post as the bot, so: - It's shown only on `/bots`, to the bot's creator and administrators. The edit page doesn't show it. - `/bots` is served with `Cache-Control: no-store` and `turbo-cache-control: no-cache`, so neither the browser nor Turbo's page cache keeps a copy. - It never appears in messages, broadcasts, redirects, flash messages or JSON. The one exception is `room.reply_to` in a webhook payload, which goes only to that bot's own webhook (see "Receiving mentions"). - Rails' parameter filter masks it (`bot_key` matches the existing `_key` filter), so `Parameters:` log lines show `[FILTERED]`. - Rails masks only the query string when it logs a path, so `lib/rails_ext/filtered_bot_path.rb` masks the code in the path too: `Started POST "/rooms/1/[FILTERED]/messages"`. `Bot.filter_path` does the same for Sentry request URLs (`config/initializers/sentry.rb`). - The code is generated by `has_secure_token` (24 base58 characters, about 140 bits) and is unique in the database. Known limits: - The code is stored in plain text, because the page has to show it again. Anyone with database access can read it. - ActiveRecord's SQL debug logging prints the value in the `bots.bot_key` query, in development or with `RAILS_LOG_LEVEL=debug`. Session tokens already appear the same way. Production logs at `info` by default. - Reverse-proxy access logs record the full path, which includes the code. Treat those logs as sensitive. Not built yet: rotating a bot code (`regenerate_bot_key` is available), rate limiting failed code attempts, per-bot scopes, and a size limit on message bodies (any size is accepted today). Known limits (webhooks): - Private and internal webhook addresses are refused, so a bot whose service runs on the same private network as Campfire can't use a webhook yet. Allowing them would be a deliberate, per-deployment decision. - Requests aren't signed, so the webhook URL is the only secret. A receiver can't tell a genuine mention from a forged POST unless the URL is secret. - There are no retries and no delivery log. A failed webhook is only logged, by class. - Sentry's HTTP breadcrumbs record a webhook's scheme, host and path (not its query) when an error is reported after a webhook call. They go to the operator's own `SENTRY_DSN`. - Replies over 64 KB are dropped, not truncated. - Edits that add a mention don't ask the bot. - Turning the switch on sends one `joined` event per open room, each a separate webhook call. There is no batching. ## Code map - `app/models/bot.rb` (credential, creator, name/avatar delegated to the user, webhook URL, `post_text`/`post_html`, `deactivate`) - `app/models/user.rb` (`has_one :bot`, `bot?`, `without_bots`, `joining_open_rooms`) - `app/models/rooms/open.rb` (grants a new open room to the people and the bots that join all open rooms) - `app/controllers/bots_controller.rb` (`/bots` management pages) - `app/controllers/bots/messages_controller.rb` (the posting API) - `app/views/bots/` (list, form, new, edit) - `lib/rails_ext/filtered_bot_path.rb` (log masking) - `db/migrate/*_create_bots.rb`, `db/migrate/*_add_webhook_url_to_bots.rb`, `db/migrate/*_add_join_all_open_rooms_to_bots.rb` - `app/models/bot/webhook.rb` (the webhook call for a mention or a join: payload, request, reply posting) - `app/jobs/bot/webhook_job.rb` (one webhook call, per bot and mention or join) - `app/jobs/room/ask_mentioned_bots_job.rb` (finds the mentioned bots for a message, one webhook job each) - `app/models/message/mentionee.rb` (`mentioned_bots`, the bots a message asks) - `app/models/room.rb` (`receive` enqueues the ask job; `memberships.grant_to` and `announce_joined_bots` send joined events) Tests: `test/models/bot_test.rb`, `test/models/bot/webhook_test.rb`, `test/models/message_test.rb` (mention cases), `test/models/room_test.rb` (joined events), `test/models/rooms/open_test.rb` (bots and new open rooms), `test/jobs/bot/webhook_job_test.rb`, `test/jobs/room/ask_mentioned_bots_job_test.rb`, `test/controllers/bots_controller_test.rb`, `test/controllers/bots/messages_controller_test.rb`, `test/lib/rails_ext/filtered_bot_path_test.rb`, plus bot cases in the accounts, users, autocomplete, messages and closed-room controller tests. bots.md development.md self-hosting.md ", "elided_chars": 6671, "warning": "Output too long." }

class Rooms::Open < Room
  after_save_commit :grant_access_to_all_users

class RoomsController < ApplicationController
  before_action :set_room, only: %i[ show destroy ]
  before_action :ensure_can_administer, only: %i[ destroy ]
  before_action :remember_last_room_visited, only: :show

  def index
    redirect_to room_url(Current.user.rooms.last)
  end

  def show
    @messages = find_messages
  end

  def destroy
    @room.destroy

    broadcast_remove_room
    redirect_to root_url
  end

  private
    def set_room
      if room = room_scope.find_by(id: params[:room_id] || params[:id])
        @room = room
      else
        redirect_to root_url, alert: "Room not found or inaccessible"
      end
    end

    # Subclasses narrow this to the room types they're allowed to act on, so that one
    # room namespace can't be used to reach another's rooms.
    def room_scope
      Current.user.rooms
    end

    def ensure_can_administer
      head :forbidden unless Current.user.can_administer?(@room)
    end

    def ensure_permission_to_create_rooms
      if Current.account.settings.restrict_room_creation_to_administrators? && !Current.user.administrator?
        head :forbidden
      end
    end

    def find_messages
      messages = @room.messages.with_creator.with_attachment_details.with_boosts

      if show_first_message = messages.find_by(id: params[:message_id])
        @messages = messages.page_around(show_first_message)
      else
        @messages = messages.last_page
      end
    end

    def room_params
      params.require(:room).permit(:name)
    end

    def broadcast_remove_room
      broadcast_remove_to :rooms, target: [ @room, :list ]
    end
end
module User::Role
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    enum :role, %i[ member administrator ]
  end

  def can_administer?(record = nil)
    administrator? || self == record&.creator || record&.new_record?
  end
end

require "test_helper"

class AccountTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "settings" do
    accounts(:signal).settings.restrict_room_creation_to_administrators = true
    assert accounts(:signal).settings.restrict_room_creation_to_administrators?
    assert_equal true, accounts(:signal)[:settings]["restrict_room_creation_to_administrators"]

    assert accounts(:signal).reload.settings.restrict_room_creation_to_administrators?

    accounts(:signal).settings.restrict_room_creation_to_administrators = false
    assert_not accounts(:signal).settings.restrict_room_creation_to_administrators?
    assert_equal false, accounts(:signal)[:settings]["restrict_room_creation_to_administrators"]
    accounts(:signal).update!(settings: { "restrict_room_creation_to_administrators" => "false" })
    assert_not accounts(:signal).reload.settings.restrict_room_creation_to_administrators?
  end

  test "logo_variant is a resized variant of a variable logo" do
    accounts(:signal).logo.attach io: file_fixture("moon.jpg").open, filename: "moon.jpg", content_type: "image/jpeg"

    assert_kind_of ActiveStorage::VariantWithRecord, accounts(:signal).logo_variant(:large)
  end

  test "logo_variant is nil when the logo cannot be resized" do
    accounts(:signal).logo.attach io: file_fixture("pixel.bmp").open, filename: "pixel.bmp", content_type: "image/bmp"

    assert_nil accounts(:signal).logo_variant(:large)
  end

  test "logo_variant is nil without a logo" do
    assert_nil accounts(:signal).logo_variant(:large)
  end
end

class BotsControllerTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  include ActionView::RecordIdentifier

  setup do
    sign_in :david
    @bot = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: users(:david))
  end

  test "index lists the bots you created with their name and bot code" do
    get bots_url

    assert_response :success
    assert_select "#bots li##{dom_id(@bot)}" do
      assert_select "strong", text: "Deploy Bot"
      assert_select "label[for=?]", dom_id(@bot, :bot_key), text: "Bot code"
      assert_select "input[id=?][readonly][value=?]", dom_id(@bot, :bot_key), @bot.bot_key
    end
  end

  test "index shows every bot on one page, without pagination" do
    12.times { |i| Bot.create!(name: "Bot #{i}", creator: users(:david)) }

    get bots_url

    assert_select "#bots li", count: 13
    assert_select "turbo-frame#next_page_container", count: 0
  end

  test "index doesn't list or expose bots created by someone else" do
    sign_in :kevin # a member, rather than an administrator who sees every bot
    get bots_url

    assert_select "strong", text: "Deploy Bot", count: 0
    assert_not_includes response.body, @bot.bot_key
  end

  test "administrators see every bot" do
    other = Bot.create!(name: "Someone Else's Bot", creator: users(:jz))

    sign_in :jason
    get bots_url

    assert_select "strong", text: "Deploy Bot"
    assert_select "strong", text: "Someone Else's Bot"
    assert_includes response.body, other.bot_key
  end

  test "index tells browsers and caches not to keep a copy of bot codes" do
    get bots_url

    assert_includes response.headers["Cache-Control"], "no-store"
  end

    assert_select "a[href=?]", edit_bot_path(@bot) do

    end
  end

  end

    assert_equal "Deploy Bot 2", bot.name
    assert_equal users(:david), bot.creator

    post bots_url, params: { bot: { name: "Deploy Bot 2" } }

    assert_not Bot.last.join_all_open_rooms?
    assert_empty Bot.last.user.rooms
  end

    post bots_url, params: { bot: { name: "Deploy Bot 2", webhook_url: "https://hooks.example.com/deploy", join_all_open_rooms: "1" } }

    bot = Bot.last

    assert_equal Rooms::Open.count, bot.user.rooms.opens.count
    assert_enqueued_jobs Rooms::Open.count, only: Bot::WebhookJob

    patch bot_url(@bot), params: { bot: { name: "Deploy Bot", join_all_open_rooms: "0" } }

    assert_not @bot.reload.join_all_open_rooms?
    assert_equal Rooms::Open.count, @bot.user.rooms.opens.count
  end

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "# The bot message API. A bot posts by sending the message text as the raw request body, e.g.
#
#   curl -d "Deploy of v1.2.3 finished ✅" https://chat.example.com/rooms/<room-id>/<bot-key>/messages
#
# There is no session here: the bot key in the path is the credential.
class Bots::MessagesController < ApplicationController
  allow_unauthenticated_access
  skip_forgery_protection

  before_action :set_bot, :set_room

  rescue_from ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound do
    head :not_found
  end

  def create
    text = message_text
    return head :unprocessable_content unless text

    @message = @bot.post_text(@room, text)

    head :created, location: message_path(@message)
  end

  # Clients send curl's default form encoding, and Rails would try to parse the body as form fields before the
  # action runs, rejecting text such as "100% done". The body is the message, so it's never read as fields.
  def process_action(...)
    request.request_parameters = {}
    super
  end

  private
    def set_bot
      @bot = Bot.active.find_by(bot_key: params[:bot_key])

      unless @bot
        response.headers["WWW-Authenticate"] = %(Bot realm="Campfire")
        head :unauthorized
      end
    end

    def set_room
      @room = @bot.user.rooms.find(params[:room_id])
    end

    # The body as text, stripped. Nil when it's blank or isn't valid UTF-8, which both count as an empty message.
    def message_text
      text = String.new(request.raw_post, encoding: Encoding::UTF_8)
      text.strip if text.valid_encoding? && text.present?
    end
end
require "test_helper"

class BotTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    @creator = users(:david)
  end

  test "creating a bot creates a user with its name, which is a bot" do
    bot = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator)

    assert_equal "Deploy Bot", bot.name
    assert_equal "Deploy Bot", bot.user.name
    assert bot.user.bot?
    assert_equal bot, bot.user.bot
  end

  test "creating a bot defaults the creator to the current user" do
    Current.set(user: @creator) do
      assert_equal @creator, Bot.create!(name: "Current Bot").creator
    end
  end

  test "a new bot joins no open rooms unless it's set to join all of them" do
    bot = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator)

    assert_not bot.join_all_open_rooms?
    assert_empty bot.user.rooms
  end

  test "a bot set to join all open rooms is a member of every open room, but not of closed rooms" do
    bot = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator, join_all_open_rooms: true)

    assert_equal Rooms::Open.count, bot.user.rooms.opens.count
    assert_not_includes bot.user.rooms, rooms(:watercooler)
  end

  test "turning the switch on adds the bot to the open rooms that exist" do
    bot = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator)

    bot.update!(join_all_open_rooms: true)

    assert_equal Rooms::Open.count, bot.user.rooms.opens.count
    assert_not_includes bot.user.rooms, rooms(:watercooler)
  end

  test "turning the switch off keeps the bot's current memberships" do
    bot = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator, join_all_open_rooms: true)

    bot.update!(join_all_open_rooms: false)

    assert_equal Rooms::Open.count, bot.user.rooms.opens.count
  end

  test "a banned bot isn't added to open rooms, even when its switch is turned on" do
    bot = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator)
    bot.user.update!(status: :banned)

    bot.update!(join_all_open_rooms: true)

    assert_empty bot.user.rooms.opens
  end

  test "turning the switch off stops the bot joining open rooms created later" do
    bot = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator, join_all_open_rooms: true)
    bot.update!(join_all_open_rooms: false)

    room = Rooms::Open.create!(name: "Later", creator: @creator)

    assert_not_includes room.users, bot.user
  end

  test "an open room created later adds the bots that join all open rooms, and no others" do
    joining = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator, join_all_open_rooms: true)
    quiet = Bot.create!(name: "Quiet Bot", creator: @creator)

    room = Rooms::Open.create!(name: "Later", creator: @creator)

    assert_includes room.users, joining.user
    assert_not_includes room.users, quiet.user
  end

  test "a closed room that becomes open adds the bots that join all open rooms" do
    joining = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator, join_all_open_rooms: true)

    room = rooms(:watercooler).becomes!(Rooms::Open)
    room.save!

    assert_includes room.users, joining.user
  end

  test "saving a bot again doesn't add it back to open rooms it was removed from" do
    bot = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator, join_all_open_rooms: true)
    room = Rooms::Open.create!(name: "Later", creator: @creator)
    assert_includes room.users, bot.user

    room.memberships.where(user: bot.user).delete_all
    bot.update!(name: "Renamed Bot")

    assert_not_includes room.users.reload, bot.user
  end

  test "a bot has a unique, unguessably long bot key" do
    first = Bot.create!(name: "First", creator: @creator)
    second = Bot.create!(name: "Second", creator: @creator)

    assert_operator first.bot_key.length, :>=, 24
    assert_not_equal first.bot_key, second.bot_key
  end

  test "a bot needs a name" do
    bot = Bot.new(creator: @creator, name: "")

    assert_not bot.valid?
    assert bot.errors.of_kind?(:name, :blank)
  end

  test "renaming and changing the avatar go through the bot's user" do
    bot = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator)

    bot.update!(name: "Renamed Bot", avatar: file_fixture("moon.jpg").open)

    assert_equal "Renamed Bot", bot.reload.user.name
    assert bot.user.avatar.attached?
  end

  test "a bot's user can't sign in, since nobody knows its password" do
    bot = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator)

    assert_not bot.user.authenticate("secret123456")
    assert_nil User.active.authenticate_by(email_address: nil, password: "secret123456")
  end

  test "a person's user isn't a bot" do
    assert_not users(:david).bot?
  end

  test "people still join every open room when they're created, unlike bots" do
    person = User.create!(name: "New Person", password: "secret123456")

    assert_equal Rooms::Open.count, person.rooms.opens.count
  end

  test "deactivating a bot deactivates its user, removes it from rooms, and deletes its bot key" do
    bot = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator, join_all_open_rooms: true)
    user = bot.user
    bot_key = bot.bot_key
    assert user.memberships.without_direct_rooms.any?

    bot.deactivate

    bot = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator)

    bot.update!(name: "Renamed Bot", avatar: file_fixture("moon.jpg").open)

    assert_equal "Renamed Bot", bot.reload.user.name
    assert bot.user.avatar.attached?
  end

    bot = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator)

    assert_not bot.user.authenticate("secret123456")
    assert_nil User.active.authenticate_by(email_address: nil, password: "secret123456")
  end

    assert_not users(:david).bot?
  end

    person = User.create!(name: "New Person", password: "secret123456")

    assert_equal Rooms::Open.count, person.rooms.opens.count
  end

  test "deactivating a bot deactivates its user, removes it from rooms, and deletes its bot key" do
    bot = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator, join_all_open_rooms: true)
    user = bot.user
    bot_key = bot.bot_key
    assert user.memberships.without_direct_rooms.any?

messages.content: The reproduction confirms the gap: there's no `bots_per_member` setting, and a member can create 8 bots. Now I'll implement, starting with the setting on `Account`. It gets a default of 5 and a validation that rejects blank or negative values. `has_json` casts blank input to `nil`, so without the check a blank field would silently disable bot creation.

arguments.command:
cd /app && cat > app/models/account.rb <<'EOF'
class Account < ApplicationRecord
  include Joinable

  has_one_attached :logo do |attachable|
    attachable.variant :large, resize_to_limit: [ 512, 512 ], format: :png
    attachable.variant :small, resize_to_limit: [ 192, 192 ], format: :png
  end

  # bots_per_member caps how many bots each member can have. Administrators aren't limited by it.
  has_json :settings, restrict_room_creation_to_administrators: false, bots_per_member: 5

  validate :bots_per_member_must_be_a_count

  def logo_variant(size)
    logo.variant(size).processed if logo.variable?
  end

  private
    # Blank input is cast to nil, and a negative count would never let anyone create a bot, so both are refused.
    def bots_per_member_must_be_a_count
      limit = settings.bots_per_member

      if limit.nil?
        errors.add :bots_per_member, :blank
      elsif limit < 0
        errors.add :bots_per_member, :greater_than_or_equal_to, count: 0
      end
    end
end
EOF

messages.content: Next are the `Bot` model tests. They cover refusal at the limit, administrators, deleted bots freeing a place, and lowering the limit without removing bots.

arguments.command:
cd /app && append_tests() { f="$1"; tail -1 "$f" | grep -qx "end" || { echo "last line not end in $f"; return 1; }; sed -i '$ d' "$f"; cat >> "$f"; echo "end" >> "$f"; }
append_tests test/models/bot_test.rb <<'EOF'

  test "a member can't create a bot past the account's bots per member" do
    kevin = users(:kevin)
    5.times { |i| Bot.create!(name: "Bot #{i}", creator: kevin) }

    error = assert_raises(ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid) do
      Bot.create!(name: "One Too Many", creator: kevin)
    end

    assert_match(/has reached the limit of 5 chat bots/, error.message)
    assert_equal 5, Bot.created_by(kevin).count
    assert_not User.exists?(name: "One Too Many")
  end

  test "administrators can create any number of bots" do
    david = users(:david)
    accounts(:signal).settings.bots_per_member = 1
    accounts(:signal).save!

    3.times { |i| Bot.create!(name: "Bot #{i}", creator: david) }

    assert_equal 3, Bot.created_by(david).count
  end

  test "deleting a bot frees a place under a member's limit" do
    kevin = users(:kevin)
    bots = 5.times.map { |i| Bot.create!(name: "Bot #{i}", creator: kevin) }
    assert_raises(ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid) { Bot.create!(name: "Sixth", creator: kevin) }

    bots.first.deactivate

    assert_nothing_raised { Bot.create!(name: "Sixth", creator: kevin) }
    assert_equal 5, Bot.created_by(kevin).count
  end

  test "lowering the limit keeps existing bots and only blocks new ones" do
    kevin = users(:kevin)
    bots = 5.times.map { |i| Bot.create!(name: "Bot #{i}", creator: kevin) }

    accounts(:signal).settings.bots_per_member = 2
    accounts(:signal).save!

    assert_equal 5, Bot.created_by(kevin).count
    assert_not kevin.can_create_bot?
    assert_raises(ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid) { Bot.create!(name: "Blocked", creator: kevin) }

    assert bots.last.update!(name: "Renamed Bot"), "editing an existing bot is still allowed"
    assert_equal "Renamed Bot", bots.last.reload.name
  end

  test "raising the limit lets a member create more bots" do
    kevin = users(:kevin)
    5.times { |i| Bot.create!(name: "Bot #{i}", creator: kevin) }

    accounts(:signal).settings.bots_per_member = 6
    accounts(:signal).save!

    assert_nothing_raised { Bot.create!(name: "Sixth", creator: kevin) }
  end

  test "a limit of zero stops members creating any bots" do
    accounts(:signal).settings.bots_per_member = 0
    accounts(:signal).save!

    assert_not users(:kevin).can_create_bot?
    assert_raises(ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid) { Bot.create!(name: "First", creator: users(:kevin)) }
  end
EOF

append_tests test/controllers/bots_controller_test.rb <<'EOF'

  test "index offers Add a chat bot to a member below the limit" do
    sign_in :kevin
    Bot.create!(name: "Bot 1", creator: users(:kevin))

    get bots_url

    assert_select "button", text: "Add a chat bot"

  test "index hides Add a chat bot from a member at the limit, and says they've reached the limit" do
    sign_in :kevin
    5.times { |i| Bot.create!(name: "Bot #{i}", creator: users(:kevin)) }

    get bots_url

    assert_select "button", text: "Add a chat bot", count: 0
    assert_select "p", text: /You’ve reached the limit of 5 chat bots/
    assert_select "#bots li", count: 5
  end

  test "index still offers Add a chat bot to administrators, who aren't limited" do
    5.times { |i| Bot.create!(name: "Bot #{i}", creator: users(:david)) }

    get bots_url

    assert_select "button", text: "Add a chat bot"
    assert_select "p", text: /reached the limit/, count: 0
  end

  test "new is forbidden to a member at the limit" do
    sign_in :kevin
    5.times { |i| Bot.create!(name: "Bot #{i}", creator: users(:kevin)) }

    get new_bot_url

    assert_response :forbidden
  end

  test "create is forbidden to a member at the limit, and creates no bot" do
    sign_in :kevin
    5.times { |i| Bot.create!(name: "Bot #{i}", creator: users(:kevin)) }

    assert_no_difference -> { Bot.count } do
      post bots_url, params: { bot: { name: "Sixth" } }
    end

    assert_response :forbidden
  end

  test "a member below the limit can create a bot" do
    sign_in :kevin
    4.times { |i| Bot.create!(name: "Bot #{i}", creator: users(:kevin)) }

    assert_difference -> { Bot.count }, +1 do
      post bots_url, params: { bot: { name: "Fifth" } }
    end

    assert_redirected_to bots_url

messages.content: I now have the real field names. I'll write a standalone browser script in `/tmp` (not in the repo). It walks the QA-facing flow: admin sets the limit, member creates bots until the limit, the button disappears, direct navigation is refused, deletion uses the native `confirm()`, and lowering the limit keeps the bots.

arguments.command:
mkdir -p /tmp/browser && cat > /tmp/browser/bots_limit_browser.rb <<'EOF'
# Throwaway browser check (not part of the repo). Drives Chromium via CDP with Cuprite, against the dev server on :3999.
require "capybara"
require "capybara/cuprite"

Capybara.register_driver(:chromium_cdp) do |app|
  Capybara::Cuprite::Driver.new(app, headless: true, window_size: [ 1280, 1000 ], browser_options: { "no-sandbox" => nil },
    timeout: 30, process_timeout: 60)
end
Capybara.default_driver = :chromium_cdp
Capybara.run_server = false
Capybara.app_host = "http://127.0.0.1:3999"
Capybara.default_max_wait_time = 10

include Capybara::DSL

$results = []
def check(label)
  ok = yield
  $results << [ ok ? "PASS" : "FAIL", label ]
  puts "#{ok ? 'PASS' : 'FAIL'}  #{label}"
rescue => e
  $results << [ "FAIL", "#{label} (#{e.class}: #{e.message.lines.first.strip})" ]
  puts "FAIL  #{label} (#{e.class}: #{e.message.lines.first.strip})"
end

def sign_in(email)
  visit "/session/new"
  fill_in "email_address", with: email
  fill_in "password", with: "secret123456"
  click_button "log_in"
  assert_no_selector "#email_address", wait: 15
end

def sign_out_everything
  Capybara.reset_sessions!
end

def set_limit_as_admin(value)
  visit "/account/edit"
  within find_field("Bots per member").ancestor("form") do
    fill_in "Bots per member", with: value
    click_button "Save changes"
  end
  assert_selector "input[name='account[settings][bots_per_member]']", wait: 10
  find_field("Bots per member").value
end

def create_bot_as_member(name)
  visit "/bots/new"
  fill_in "Name the bot", with: name
  click_button "Save changes"
end

# 1. Administrator sees the setting with the default of 5 and saves a new value.
sign_in "david@37signals.com"
visit "/account/edit"
check("admin sees 'Bots per member' labelled input with default 5") do
  find_field("Bots per member").value == "5" && find_field("Bots per member")[:type] == "number"
end
page.save_screenshot("/tmp/browser/1_admin_account_default.png")

check("admin saves 'Bots per member' = 3 with Save changes") do
  value = set_limit_as_admin("3")
  value == "3"
end

# 2. A member (Kevin) can create bots up to the limit, then the page says so.
sign_out_everything
sign_in "kevin@37signals.com"
check("member doesn't see the bots per member field on account settings") do
  visit "/account/edit"
  has_no_field?("Bots per member")
end

check("member creates 3 bots via the form") do
  3.times { |i| create_bot_as_member("Kevin Bot #{i + 1}") }
  visit "/bots"
  has_selector?("#bots li", count: 3)
end

visit "/bots"
check("at the limit, 'Add a chat bot' is not offered") do
  has_no_button?("Add a chat bot")
end
check("at the limit, the page says they've 'reached the limit'") do
  has_text?("reached the limit of 3 chat bots")
end
page.save_screenshot("/tmp/browser/2_member_at_limit.png")

check("at the limit, the new bot form is refused (403)") do
  visit "/bots/new"
  page.status_code == 403
end

check("at the limit, the new bot page doesn't render the form") do
  visit "/bots/new"
  has_no_field?("Name the bot")
end

# 3. Deleting a bot (native confirm) frees a slot.
visit "/bots"
check("delete asks with the native confirm() dialog, and deletes the bot") do
  visit "/bots"
  first("#bots li a[href$='/edit']").click
  message = nil
  accept_confirm(wait: 10) do
    message = nil
    click_button "Delete this chat bot"
  end
  has_current_path?("/bots", wait: 10) && has_selector?("#bots li", count: 2)
end

check("after deleting one, 'Add a chat bot' is offered again") do
  visit "/bots"
  has_button?("Add a chat bot") && has_no_text?("reached the limit")
end

check("a member can create a bot again after deleting one") do
  create_bot_as_member("Kevin Bot 4")
  visit "/bots"
  has_selector?("#bots li", count: 3) && has_no_button?("Add a chat bot")
end

# 4. Lowering the limit keeps existing bots and blocks new ones.
sign_out_everything
sign_in "david@37signals.com"
check("admin lowers 'Bots per member' to 1") do
  set_limit_as_admin("1") == "1"
end

sign_out_everything
sign_in "kevin@37signals.com"
visit "/bots"
check("lowering the limit keeps the 3 existing bots listed") do
  has_selector?("#bots li", count: 3)
end
check("lowered limit: message says the limit is 1 chat bot, no 'Add a chat bot'") do
  has_text?("reached the limit of 1 chat bot.") && has_no_button?("Add a chat bot")
end
page.save_screenshot("/tmp/browser/3_member_lowered_limit.png")

# 5. Blank value is blocked by the browser's required field, so nothing is saved.
sign_out_everything
sign_in "david@37signals.com"
check("a blank 'Bots per member' is not submitted (required), value is kept at 1") do
  visit "/account/edit"
  fill_in "Bots per member", with: ""
  find_field("Bots per member").ancestor("form").click_button("Save changes")
  sleep 1
  visit "/account/edit"
  find_field("Bots per member").value == "1"
end

check("admin 'Bots per member' has min=0 and step=1 for the browser to enforce") do
  visit "/account/edit"
  field = find_field("Bots per member")
  field[:min] == "0" && field[:step] == "1" && field[:required]
end
page.save_screenshot("/tmp/browser/4_admin_account_saved.png")

# 6. Restore the default so the dev data is back to normal.
check("admin restores the default of 5") do
  set_limit_as_admin("5") == "5"
end

puts "\n#{$results.count { |r| r[0] == 'PASS' }} passed, #{$results.count { |r| r[0] == 'FAIL' }} failed"
EOF

Who sees and manages what:

- Administrators see and manage every bot.

Bots do not join open rooms by default, unlike people. The "Add to all open rooms" switch makes a bot a member of every
open room: the rooms that exist when the switch is turned on, and each open room created later. Turning the switch off
keeps the bot in the rooms it is already in, and only stops new open rooms from adding it. Bots can be added to closed
rooms the same way people are (the access switches in the room's settings).

A bot that is not in a room can't post there: the message endpoint answers `404 Not Found` (see "Posting messages").

row. The user holds the bot's name, avatar and room memberships, so everything that handles people (membership,
mentions, messages, push, avatars) works for bots without changes. The credential lives only in `bots`, so it
never appears when users are serialized or listed.

**Bot users can't sign in.** The `users.password_digest` column is `NOT NULL`, so a bot's user gets a random
password that nobody learns. A bot has no email address, and its profile doesn't offer the auto-login link.

**Deleting a bot** deactivates its user, the same way removing a person does: the user leaves every room (direct
rooms excepted), and its messages stay. The `bots` row is destroyed, which kills the bot code. Deactivated and
banned users fail authentication too (`Bot.active`).

## Limiting bots per member

Administrators set **Bots per member** on the account settings page (`/account/edit`, shown to administrators only).
It's a whole number, 5 by default. Zero is allowed; blank and negative values are refused.

- A member can have at most that many bots. A bot counts until it's deleted, so deleting one frees its place.
- Administrators aren't limited.
- At the limit, `/bots` doesn't offer "Add a chat bot" and says "You’ve reached the limit of 5 chat bots". Opening
  `/bots/new` and posting to `/bots` both answer `403 Forbidden`. The bot model refuses the creation as well, so no
  other path can create a bot past the limit.
- Lowering the limit never removes bots. A member keeps every bot they have, can still edit and delete them, and can't
  add more until they're under the new limit. Raising the limit lets them add more.

EOF

messages.content:
The per-member bot limit is implemented, tested, and checked in a real browser. The full suite passes (481 runs, 0 failures, same 22 DNS-only skips as before), rubocop is clean, and Brakeman reports 0 warnings.

## What changed

**Setting.** `Account` gets `bots_per_member` (default 5) in its `has_json` settings, next to `restrict_room_creation_to_administrators`. A validation refuses blank and negative values; zero is allowed.

**Rule.** `User#can_create_bot?` returns true for administrators. For members it counts their existing `Bot` rows, which are the same rows the bots page lists, and compares that with the limit. A deleted bot has no row, so it doesn't count.

**Enforcement.**
- `Bot` has a create-only validation, so every creation path is refused, including console and any future code. It runs inside the save transaction, and the app's SQLite transactions use immediate mode, so two rapid creates by one member can't both pass the count.
- `BotsController` refuses `new` and `create` with 403 at the limit, the same way room creation is refused under the admin-only restriction.
- Updates and deletes are never blocked, so lowering the limit keeps existing bots.

**UI.**
- `/account/edit`: an admin-only "Bots per member" number field (`min=0`, `step=1`, `required`).
- `/bots`: "Add a chat bot" is replaced at the limit by "You’ve reached the limit of N chat bots. Delete one to add another, or ask an administrator to raise the limit."

**Docs.** `docs/bots.md` has a new "Limiting bots per member" section, a design note on the rule and its race safety, and updated code map and test lists.

## Decisions to review

- **Refusal status is 403, not a redirect**, to match existing refusals in the codebase.
- **The field sits inside the existing account-name form.** I first put it in its own form, which gave the page two "Save changes" buttons and would make QA clicks on that label ambiguous. Now there's one button, and both fields save together.
- **Banned bots still count.** They're still listed on `/bots` and can be deleted there, so counting them matches what the member sees.

## Verification

- **Tests:** 27 new tests across the account, user, bot model, bots controller and accounts controller tests.
- **Reproduction:** before the change, a member created 8 bots and the setting didn't exist. After the change, the 6th is refused.
- **Browser:** Rails system tests can't run here (no `chromedriver`, and no network to download one). Instead I drove Chromium through Cuprite against a dev server. 16 checks passed: the labelled field and its default, a member at the limit with no button, the "reached the limit" text, the 403 on `/bots/new`, deletion via the native `confirm()` freeing a slot, lowering the limit keeping bots, and blank input being blocked. I also checked over HTTP that `POST /bots` returns 403 at the limit.
- **Layout:** measured with no overflow. I couldn't view screenshots directly.

I haven't committed anything. The bot feature was already uncommitted in the working tree, and my changes sit on top of it. I removed the dev database and stopped the dev server afterwards.
